findings: A (Hojden minskar lika mycket) - killed by ”Storlekarna följer ingen jämn trappa.”
C (mest mellan de tva nedersta) - killed by ”mellan de två nedersta raderna skiljer det åtta tiondels millimeter” (0,8 mm, the smallest step on the sheet).

justification: Arithmetic: 73->36 = 37 mm, the largest absolute drop, and -50% the largest relative one; the bottom step is 0,8 mm / -10%. B wins on both readings, so there is no absolute-vs-relative ambiguity.

findings: A (typografin tar redan hansyn) - killed by ”Med den regeln blir arkets typografi ett mätfel.”
B (forsamrar ogats upplosning) - killed by ”Den sitter inte i ögats upplösning: näthinnan skiljer ut tecknet, men det arbete som ska avgöra vilken bokstav det är störs av grannarna.”

justification: C is the relative-spacing rule stated twice (the ratio rule, then its application to the bottom rows). D is its verbatim mirror image, B is refuted by the explicit 'not resolution' sentence, A by 'ett matfel'.

findings: A (raden provas om) - killed by ”Ingen rad prövas om”
B (fjorton rader las igenom) - killed by ”Det är inte de fjorton raderna som tar tid”

The nearest stated refutations are the explicit not-X-but-Y attribution ”Det är inte de fjorton raderna som tar tid, utan de sjuttio tecknen”, ”sköterskan går vidare så snart tecknet är sagt” and ”Även ett barn som stannar högt upp tar längre tid än förut” (so the extra time is not located at the bottom). Suggest making C explicitly contradict a stated span if a harder kill is wanted.
Key D stands on ”vart och ett ska höras och prickas av” and ”tecknen ovanför också ska prickas av ett och ett”
justification: D paraphrases the stated cause verbatim; no second option is supportable. Timing reconciles: 40 barn x 3 min = 120 min = tva timmar, and 120/7 = 17,1 -> sjutton.

findings: B (barnens syn forbattrades) - killed by ”Som en enda kurva över barns syn i en svensk stad går den inte att läsa.”
C (gransen 0,8 sanktes) - killed by ”Gränsen 0,8 ändrades inte vid bytet”

Key A stands on ”Den kommer inte som en lutning över några år, utan mellan två på varandra följande årgångar.” plus ”Nedgången i kurvan ligger på det året.”
justification: Dates reconcile: 1961-1996 = 36 argangar; 17 first (1961-1977) + 19 following (1978-1996) = 36, and the new sheet went up under hostterminen 1978, so the break falls exactly at the 17/19 seam.

findings: A (dela lika) - killed by ”Delar vi fyrtiofem lika på tio bilar blir det fyra och en halv på var, och då laddar ingen av de tio.”
B (hoj huvudsakringen forst) - killed by ”Någon större huvudsäkring tänker jag därför inte begära i år.”

Amperage reconciles throughout: 125-80=45; 45/6=7,5 so sju bilar; 45/8=5,6 below the 6 A floor; 4x32=128 vs 45 available, hence 'snabba bara sa lange tre av dem star tomma'.

findings: A (bakom glas i entren) - killed by ”Kallelsen sitter med häftstift på anslagstavlan utanför tvättstugan”

findings: A (halla obehoriga ute) - killed by ”Ett räcke i knähöjd är inte byggt för att hålla någon ute”
B (byttes ofta) - killed by ”Räcket är det ursprungliga.”
C (omalat pa bada sidor) - killed by ”Insidan har sin gamla gröna färg i behåll.”

findings: B (stolpe mitt pa golvet) - killed by ”Banan ligger under bar himmel, utan tak och utan stolpar inne på golvet.”
C (hora spelmannen lika bra) - killed by ”längst bort på banan hördes de sämre”

Key A stands on ”paren går åt samma håll, motsols” and ”Rundningen var inte det billiga valet: den kostade virke”
justification: A carries two claims and the passage states both: one-way traffic in a band along the edge, and the round form as the more expensive choice. D is the only option whose kill depends on a physical detail rather than a purpose statement, but 'plant' plus 'rinner ner mellan bradorna' states it outright.

findings: A (they fall as the warning weakens; eleven is good) - killed by "three at the cottage nearest the vessel, five at the farm office halfway up, eleven at the bungalow" (they rise) and "He is working to four" (eleven fails).

B (he counts quarter-turns) - killed by the definition "the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything"; the quarter-turns are how he opens the valve, not what is recorded.
D (worked out from pipe length) - killed by the same definition plus "sniffs at the funnel until the smell arrives": the figure is measured at the box, not computed.
Key C stands on "The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air"
justification: Threshold reconciles with the stated target: four parts per thousand = 0,4%, and propane's lean limit is about 2% by volume, so four is indeed 'a fifth of the leanest mixture'.

findings: B (added at the estate) - killed by "put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume"
D (reaches the house intact, lost at the cooker) - killed by "the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in"

C (clings to the wall once the steel has begun to corrode IN SERVICE) - CLOSEST CALL. Its core is true ("Some of the mercaptan simply sticks to it"); only the temporal clause is refuted, by "a bloom of rust from the weeks the lengths stood in the yard" (the oxide predates service), "a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service", "Age works the other way about." and "The pipe that needs watching is the pipe nobody has ever used." REPAIR REQUEST: a hurried solver can read C as the stated sticking mechanism. Recommend rewording C so the falsified part is the load-bearing part, e.g. 'It clings to the wall more and more as the main ages in service' - that is killed head-on by 'Age works the other way about.'
Key A stands on "Some is oxidised on contact into a disulphide, a serviceable molecule that is no use as a warning, because it hardly smells."
justification: A is a near-verbatim paraphrase and is the answer; C is not defensible once the 'in service' clause is read, but it is the one option in this unit whose kill rests on a qualifier rather than on its main claim.

findings: A (short enough) - killed by "is longer than the new run"
B (narrower bore) - killed by "is the same bore"
C (its own vessel) - killed by "comes off the same vessel and the same fill"
Key D stands on "Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking, and the gas goes past unchanged." applied to "reads three at both ends"
justification: The sentence is built as a controlled comparison: longer, same bore, same vessel, same fill - so only saturation with age is left, and 'three at both ends' matches the baseline figure at the cottage nearest the vessel. Clean inference item.

findings: A (ordinary dose, date fixed in advance) - killed twice: "holding the system at three or four times the ordinary dose" and "What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance."
C (main cost is the odorant) - killed by "costs more than the odorant does" and by "an unbudgeted tanker movement"
D (carried out once the houses are in use) - killed by "you do it before the first burner is lit"

Key B stands on "The soak ends when the readings say it has ended, which means walking the run again." REPAIR REQUEST: B says 'a SECOND walk', but the closing scene shows the second walk in progress reading six against a target of four, i.e. the second walk does not end it. Recommend 'a further walk of the run' or 'another walk of the run' so the key cannot be rejected on the ordinal.

Also note: 'the smell has come back' renders 'the readings say it has ended' only indirectly (low readings = the warning gets through). It holds, but a literal reader may hesitate because the village is stated to be smelling gas throughout the soak ("a fortnight in which a village that has never smelled gas smells gas").
justification: A, C and D are hard-killed, so B is the only survivor and is supportable; the flag is about wording that could push an exact reader toward NONE_DEFENSIBLE, not about the key being wrong.

findings: A (it stands) - killed by "Thursday has moved to the Thursday after."
B (given up) - killed by the same sentence: a new dated Thursday is named, not abandonment.
C (most houses on the old date) - killed by the same sentence read against "the twenty-six houses above it are due to be lit on Thursday": one date for all twenty-six, and that date moved.
Key D stands on "The heavy dose went into the vessel on Monday and the run has been held at it since." plus the moved Thursday = one week.
justification: Thursday to the Thursday after is exactly a week, and 'has been held at it since' gives the second half of D. Note B and C lean on the same single sentence; each is genuinely contradicted by it, but the item has only one refuting span for three options.

findings: A (Nowadays) - killed by "nothing modern about it either"
B (Oddly) - killed by "There is nothing unusual in that house": the essay's thesis is that the failure is ordinary, not strange.
C (Happily) - wrong polarity, killed by "The hall carpet took most of the damage."
Key D (Worse) stands on the escalation into "they had lived there eleven years, which is long enough to have asked"
justification: The second paragraph's opening sentence is doing double duty as the kill for both A and B, which is a tidy design. D is the idiomatic sentence adverb for the aggravating fact.

findings: B (recruit) - killed by "This competence is not earned and not handed out." - nobody enlists the holder.
C (caretaker) - killed by "The knowledge holds no office and is not bought with the house."
D (lodger) - killed by "It may sit with the owner, the owner’s daughter, or the man who rents the back bedroom.": the lodger is only one of three named possibilities.
Key A (witness) stands on the appositive "somebody who was in the right room on the right morning and has answered questions ever since"
justification: The colon defines the gap word as accidental presence plus subsequent testimony, which is a witness and nothing else on the list.

findings: A (issued) - killed by "not earned and not handed out"
C (bought) - killed by "is not bought with the house"
D (chosen) - killed by the simile in the gap sentence itself, "the way a cold is, by being in the room when it happens": a cold is not chosen.
Key B (caught) is the fixed collocation with the same simile.
justification: 'Caught, the way a cold is' is the only idiomatic completion and the two nearest rivals are refuted by the preceding paragraph's explicit denials.

findings: C (opinion) - killed by "nobody disputes them"
D (anecdote) - killed by "most are four words long" and by "It names one thing in one building and explains nothing": an anecdote is a story, not a four-word name.

B (instance) - INFERENCE-LEAN REJECTION: no span contradicts it outright. It is rejected on fit - 'Each item is an instance' is incomplete English (an instance of what?), it does not NAME anything, and 'instance' presupposes the general type the essay denies exists ("no rule, no principle, nothing that carries to another house"). Recommend replacing B with a noun the passage kills outright if a stated refutation is wanted.
Key A (address) stands on "It names one thing in one building and explains nothing", which is a definition of an address.
justification: A is clearly best and B is not really defensible, but B is the one option in this unit I can only reject on collocation and on the type/token argument rather than on a stated contradiction.

findings: A (privileged) - killed by "nothing on it is being kept back" and "Ask, and you will be told gladly and at length"
D (technical) - killed by "Nothing on that list is difficult"

B (perishable) - rejected on the concessive frame, not on content: the sentence is "Although the whole of it is entirely" ... "it moves one way only", and perishability does not concede against one-way transmission. Note that the essay does support perishability elsewhere ("A departure is therefore the dangerous event"), so a solver who reads for theme rather than for the connective could be drawn to it. Worth watching.
Key C (commonplace) stands on "Nothing on that list is difficult and nothing on it is being kept back." and on "In almost any house, one person knows"
justification: The 'Although X, yet one way only' frame requires X to be something that would predict easy spread: easy and freely given = commonplace. B is thematically true of the subject but structurally wrong for the slot.

findings: A (meter sampled only the middle; curve stops there) - killed on both clauses by "she played a dozen notes into her meter, the last of them from the top octave, and it drew her a curve for all eighty-eight notes"

B (small instrument loses more than the figure allows for) - killed by "this upright’s figure is larger than a grand’s, its short thick strings already counted in it" and by "The curve’s right about the wire"
C (allowance for the cold) - killed by "The extra cents are not an allowance for the cold"
Key D stands on "The last octave comes in over somebody’s left hand, two octaves down, and that’s what it has to agree with."
justification: All three non-keys are pre-refuted by explicit denials placed for that purpose; the fourth-partial figure (two octaves up, about nine cents) reconciles with the stretch described.

findings: B (the coach road settled who went on the card) - killed by "The Shenwolds sit three miles off that road, up a lane the coaches did not use." while the card still gives "Thursdays at Upper and Lower Shenwold"
C (Thursday shared because each holds a market that day) - killed by "Upper Shenwold has no market of its own."
D (Nerresby drew the biggest crowd) - killed by "the Thursday market is the largest of the four"

Key A stands on the day-by-day match: "Haddenthorpe has kept its Monday market since a charter of 1227, and Nerresby has held a Tuesday one for as long." and "Thrapmere fills on a Wednesday and Lower Shenwold on a Thursday", against the card's "Mondays at Haddenthorpe, Tuesdays at Nerresby, Wednesdays at Thrapmere, Thursdays at Upper and Lower Shenwold"
justification: Mileages reconcile exactly: Nerresby-Haddenthorpe 9 + Haddenthorpe-Thrapmere 21 = the stated 30 from Nerresby to Thrapmere. Chronology supports A over B: the markets are chartered 1227 and the turnpike dates from 1769, so the days cannot have been set by the road.

findings: Key C stated: "The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air: the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything."

A killed by stated direction of the gradient: "three at the cottage nearest the vessel, five at the farm office halfway up, eleven at the bungalow" read against "the further it has travelled against that wall, the less it has" - the figure RISES as the warning weakens, so eleven is the worst reading on the sheet, not a good one.
A also killed against the stated threshold: "He is working to four, a fifth of the leanest mixture of propane and air that will burn" - eleven is nearly three times the working limit.

B killed by stated unit of the record: the quarter-turn is the method of opening ("opens its needle valve a quarter-turn at a time") while the recorded figure is a dilution in parts per thousand, per the span quoted above.

D killed by stated counterexample: "The old steel line that has fed the farm buildings since the sixties is longer than the new run, is the same bore, comes off the same vessel and the same fill, and reads three at both ends." - a longer line reads lower, so the figure is not computed from length.

Arithmetic reconciles: the box reads parts of gas per thousand parts of air, so four parts/thousand = 0.4 percent; a fifth of propane's leanest burnable mixture (~2.1 percent by volume) = 0.42 percent = ~4 parts/thousand. The stated threshold 'four' and the stated identity 'a fifth of the leanest mixture' agree to within rounding, and match real odorisation practice (detection at 1/5 LEL).

Gradient reconciles with the threshold and with the ending: 3 (nearest, passes 4), 5 (halfway, fails), 11 (head of lane, fails); after the soak the re-walk reads "The figure he writes down is six." - still above four, i.e. improved but not finished, which is consistent with the stated rule that the soak ends when the readings say so.
No inference-only rejection in this item.
justification: C is the only option matching the stated definition of the recorded number; A inverts the stated direction of the slope and misreads eleven against the stated threshold of four; B misnames the unit; D is refuted by the farm line, which is longer yet reads three.

findings: Key A stated: "Some is oxidised on contact into a disulphide, a serviceable molecule that is no use as a warning, because it hardly smells."
B killed by stated place of dosing: "a sulphur compound put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume"
D killed by stated loss in transit: "the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in"

HARD CALL - C is the nearest miss and is killed only on its timing clause. Sticking to the wall IS stated ("Some of the mercaptan simply sticks to it."), but C attributes it to steel that "has begun to corrode in service", which the passage contradicts twice: the oxide is already present on a NEW main ("The inside of a new steel main is not the smooth tube it looks: it carries mill scale from the rolling and a bloom of rust from the weeks the lengths stood in the yard", i.e. formed in the yard before service) and uptake FALLS with service age ("Bare oxide takes the most, so a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service"; "Age works the other way about."). The kill is on stated spans, not on inference, but a careless reader can reach C; flag for distractor review only, not a key defect.
justification: A is stated verbatim. C is a near-miss whose only defect is the in-service timing of the corrosion, which the passage explicitly places in the yard before service and explicitly says decreases with age; B and D are directly contradicted.

findings: Key D stated: "Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking, and the gas goes past unchanged." applied to "The old steel line that has fed the farm buildings since the sixties is longer than the new run, is the same bore, comes off the same vessel and the same fill, and reads three at both ends." - equal readings at both ends mean no further uptake.
A killed by stated length: "is longer than the new run"
B killed by stated bore: "is the same bore"
C killed by stated source: "comes off the same vessel and the same fill"

The three wrong options are each killed by one clause of the same sentence, which is a clean elimination design; the reading 'three at both ends' also reconciles with the working threshold of four (the old line passes everywhere).
No inference-only rejection in this item.
justification: D follows from the stated saturation rule plus the flat three-at-both-ends reading; A, B and C each contradict an explicit clause of the sentence that describes the farm line.

findings: Key B stated: "The soak ends when the readings say it has ended, which means walking the run again." - the end is fixed by a further walk with the box, not by a date.
A killed twice: dose - "holding the system at three or four times the ordinary dose until it will take no more"; date - "What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance."

C killed by stated cost comparison: "one call-out to a kitchen where the cooker is off and the smell is only the soak costs more than the odorant does" and by the listed bill "several days of gas, an unbudgeted tanker movement"
D killed by stated sequencing: "you do it before the first burner is lit"

WATCH ITEM (non-blocking): B's gloss "shows that the smell has come back" is a paraphrase of "The soak ends when the readings say it has ended" - during the soak the village is smelling gas, so 'come back' has to be read as 'the warning survives to the far end again'. That reading is supported by "the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in". B's "a second walk" is also slightly over-specified against "walking the run again", since the closing reading of six is still above the stated working figure of four and implies at least one further walk. Neither point makes any other option defensible; B is the only survivor.
No inference-only rejection: all three wrong options are killed by stated spans.
justification: B is the only option consistent with the stated end condition; A, C and D each contradict an explicit clause. B's wording is a loose paraphrase but the alternative readings are all foreclosed by the passage.

findings: Key D stated: "The heavy dose went into the vessel on Monday and the run has been held at it since. Thursday has moved to the Thursday after." - one week, dose still held.
A killed by the same span: the date did not stand, it moved.
B killed by the existence of a named new date ("Thursday has moved to the Thursday after"), so it was rescheduled rather than abandoned.

C killed by the stated single date for the whole run: "the twenty-six houses above it are due to be lit on Thursday" - one date covers all twenty-six, and that date moved as a whole; the passage never splits the run. This is the weakest of the three kills in this item (the split is contradicted by the one-date framing rather than denied word for word), but it is still anchored on stated text, not on silence.

Date arithmetic: dose in on Monday, original light-up the following Thursday, new light-up the Thursday after that = a slip of exactly seven days, matching D's "slipped by a week". Note the soft tension (not a contradiction) with "a fortnight in which a village that has never smelled gas smells gas": the smell period is longer than the seven-day slip, but the passage explicitly refuses to date the end ("What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance.") and the closing reading of six against the working figure of four leaves the new Thursday in doubt by design.
justification: D restates the two stated facts of the final paragraph; A contradicts the move, B ignores the named replacement date, C invents a split of a run the passage lights on one date.

findings: Gap (1) frame: "none could say which side of the path. ___(1)___, they had lived there eleven years, which is long enough to have asked."
Key D 'Worse' works as an escalating comment adverb: the eleven years aggravate the failure just described, and the paragraph closes on the cost "The hall carpet took most of the damage."

HARD CALL - B 'Oddly' is the one live rival, since it is also a comment disjunct and the eleven-years fact could be called strange. It is killed by the essay's own stated thesis in the very next sentence: "There is nothing unusual in that house, and nothing modern about it either." The author's position is that this ignorance is ordinary, so labelling it odd contradicts stated text. I record this as a kill on stated text, but it is the thinnest margin in the batch and depends on reading the following paragraph.
A 'Nowadays' killed by the same stated span: "nothing modern about it either" - the piece explicitly refuses a then-versus-now framing.
C 'Happily' killed by the stated outcome: "The hall carpet took most of the damage." and "for eight minutes none of the three adults living there could turn the water off"
justification: D is the escalation the sentence needs. B is defeated only by the immediately following denial that anything here is unusual - defensible-looking on a local read, foreclosed on a full read; A and C are contradicted outright.

findings: Key A 'witness' is fixed by the appositive: "somebody who was in the right room on the right morning and has answered questions ever since"
C 'caretaker' killed by stated absence of any office: "The knowledge holds no office and is not bought with the house."
D 'lodger' killed by the stated range of holders: "It may sit with the owner, the owner’s daughter, or the man who rents the back bedroom." - the lodger is only one of three named possibilities.
B 'recruit' killed by stated mode of acquisition: "This competence is not earned and not handed out." and "by being in the room when it happens"
All four options take 'a' rather than 'an', so the article leaks nothing.
justification: The appositive defines a witness exactly - present at the event, answering questions ever since. The other three each import an office, a tenancy or a selection that the passage denies.

findings: Key B 'caught' is fixed by the simile: "the way a cold is, by being in the room when it happens"
A 'issued' killed by "This competence is not earned and not handed out."
C 'bought' killed by "is not bought with the house"
D 'chosen' killed by the same 'not earned and not handed out' span plus the simile - a cold is not chosen.
No inference-only rejection in this item.
justification: Only 'caught' collocates with the stated cold simile, and each rival is negated word for word elsewhere in the passage.

findings: Gap (4) frame: "Each item is an ___(4)___. It names one thing in one building and explains nothing; most are four words long; nobody disputes them."
Key A 'address': a locator that names one thing in one building and carries no explanation, matching "the one behind the coats" as the worked example.
B 'instance' killed by the stated denial of any general rule it could instantiate: "there is nothing in it to have: no rule, no principle, nothing that carries to another house"
C 'opinion' killed by "nobody disputes them"
D 'anecdote' killed by the stated length and by the absence of narrative: "most are four words long" and "explains nothing"
All four options begin with a vowel, so the stated article 'an' leaks nothing.
justification: 'Address' is the only noun that names one thing in one building while explaining nothing; 'instance' presupposes the rule the passage denies, 'opinion' the dispute it denies, and 'anecdote' a length it denies.

findings: Gap (5) frame: "Although the whole of it is entirely ___(5)___, it moves one way only: one body pointing and another beside it, looking where the first points."

Key C 'commonplace' supplies the concession the 'Although' needs, and is set up by "Nothing on that list is difficult and nothing on it is being kept back." and "Ask, and you will be told gladly and at length, and still have nothing."
A 'privileged' killed by "nothing on it is being kept back"
D 'technical' killed by "Nothing on that list is difficult" and by "no rule, no principle"

B 'perishable' killed by the stated permanence in the holder: "whoever is in the hall then has the fact for good – twenty years on, in the dark, first go". It also fails the concessive: perishability would agree with one-way transmission rather than contrast with it.
justification: 'Commonplace' is the only reading that makes the 'Although' a genuine concession; the other three are each contradicted by a stated clause about the knowledge being easy, unguarded and permanently held.

findings: Key D stated: "The last octave comes in over somebody’s left hand, two octaves down, and that’s what it has to agree with."

A killed by the stated sampling and coverage: "Before starting she played a dozen notes into her meter, the last of them from the top octave, and it drew her a curve for all eighty-eight notes from this piano’s own figure." - the sample reaches the top octave and the curve covers all eighty-eight notes.
B killed by 'already counted in': "so this upright’s figure is larger than a grand’s, its short thick strings already counted in it"
C killed outright: "The extra cents are not an allowance for the cold: a winter takes the whole instrument down together, and that is another visit."

Physics reconciles: "A note down in the tenor has its fourth partial about nine cents sharp, and that is where the treble note two octaves above it goes, nine cents wide of the arithmetic." - the fourth partial is exactly two octaves above the fundamental, so the nine cents transfers correctly; the two-to-three cents of extra stretch in the top octave and a half is a smaller, separate quantity and does not collide with the nine.
No inference-only rejection in this item.
justification: D is the tuner's stated reason in her own words; A, B and C are each negated by an explicit clause (top-octave sample and all-88 curve; stiffness already in the figure; cold explicitly excluded).

findings: Key A: every day on the card matches that place's market day, stated four times - "Haddenthorpe has kept its Monday market since a charter of 1227, and Nerresby has held a Tuesday one for as long." and "Thrapmere fills on a Wednesday and Lower Shenwold on a Thursday" against "Mondays at Haddenthorpe, Tuesdays at Nerresby, Wednesdays at Thrapmere, Thursdays at Upper and Lower Shenwold."

B killed by a stated counterexample on the card itself: "The Shenwolds sit three miles off that road, up a lane the coaches did not use." - the Thursday stop is on the card yet off the coach road, so the road did not settle inclusion. The charter dates also predate the turnpike ("a charter of 1227" versus "turnpiked in 1769").
C killed by "Upper Shenwold has no market of its own."
D killed by "the Thursday market is the largest of the four."

Mileage reconciles exactly: "Nerresby stands nine miles from Haddenthorpe." plus "the road to it runs back through Haddenthorpe and twenty-one miles beyond" gives 9 + 21 = 30, matching "Thrapmere stands thirty miles from Nerresby". The Tuesday-to-Wednesday leg therefore doubles back past Monday's town, which is the geometry that shows market days rather than travel economy set the order - the support A needs.

The Shenwold distances are consistent: four miles from Haddenthorpe with three miles of that up a side lane leaves a junction about a mile out of the town, and "ten minutes’ walk from each other" fits two villages sharing one Thursday stop.
No inference-only rejection: each wrong option is killed by a stated sentence.
justification: All four card days coincide with stated market days, and the 30-mile Tuesday-to-Wednesday backtrack rules out a distance-driven order; B, C and D are each contradicted outright.

findings: Nyckel B stod uttryckt: "Den översta bokstaven är 73 millimeter, nästa rad 36 och den därefter 24." och "Det första steget halverar alltså bokstavshöjden, det sista ändrar den med en tiondel." - 73 till 36 är 37 mm och en halvering, största steget både absolut och relativt.
A dödad av "Storlekarna följer ingen jämn trappa."
C dödad av "mellan de två nedersta raderna skiljer det åtta tiondels millimeter" - 0,8 mm är det minsta steget, inte det största.
D dödad av "Sedan blir stegen kortare" - stegen krymper nedåt, så mitten kan inte ha det största steget.

Radräkningen stämmer: 1+2+3+5+6+7+8+8 = 40 bokstäver på åtta rader, vilket matchar "Tavlan är ett ark med fyrtio bokstäver fördelade på åtta rader." och "på var och en av de två nedersta raderna står åtta bokstäver"

Storleksstegen stämmer mot visusdefinitionen: 73 mm på fem meter motsvarar visus 0,1, 36 mm motsvarar 0,2 (läsbar på tjugofem meter, som texten själv säger), 24 mm motsvarar 0,3, och nedersta raden "de minsta drygt sju millimeter höga" motsvarar 1,0 - vilket också är den fysikaliskt korrekta siffran (5 m gånger 5 bågminuter = 7,3 mm). Sista steget: 0,8 mm på cirka 8,1 mm är en tiondel, precis som texten säger.
Ingen dödsdom vilar enbart på slutledning i denna fråga.
justification: B följer av de utsatta höjderna 73-36-24 och av den uttryckta beskrivningen av första och sista steget; A, C och D motsägs var för sig av en utskriven sats.

findings: Nyckel C stod uttryckt: "Hur stor störningen blir beror inte på hur många millimeter som skiljer tecknen åt, utan på hur stort det avståndet är i förhållande till tecknet självt." med tillämpningen "mellanrummen mellan dem blir därför små i förhållande till tecknen"
A dödad av "Med den regeln blir arkets typografi ett mätfel." och "Raderna sattes en gång så att de fyllde papperets bredd."
B dödad av "Den sitter inte i ögats upplösning: näthinnan skiljer ut tecknet, men det arbete som ska avgöra vilken bokstav det är störs av grannarna."
D dödad av "Trängseln växer alltså nedåt på arket i takt med att bokstäverna krymper." - D vänder riktningen.
Ingen dödsdom vilar enbart på slutledning i denna fråga.
justification: C är regeln som texten formulerar ordagrant; A, B och D motsäger var sin utskriven sats om typografin, om ögats upplösning respektive om riktningen.

findings: Nyckel D stod uttryckt: "Det är inte de fjorton raderna som tar tid, utan de sjuttio tecknen: vart och ett ska höras och prickas av."
A dödad av "Ingen rad prövas om"
B dödad av samma nyckelsats: raderna pekas uttryckligen ut som det som inte tar tid.

C dödad av "Även ett barn som stannar högt upp tar längre tid än förut, eftersom tecknen ovanför också ska prickas av ett och ett." - tidsåtgången hänger inte på de nedersta tecknen, och texten säger tvärtom "sköterskan går vidare så snart tecknet är sagt". Detta är den minst ordagranna av de tre dödsdomarna, men den vilar på utskriven text, inte på tystnad.

Siffrorna går ihop: fjorton rader gånger fem bokstäver ger sjuttio tecken ("Varje rad har fem bokstäver, varken fler eller färre, och raderna är fjorton."), och en bokstav värd "en femtedel av steget mellan två rader" stämmer med fem bokstäver per rad.

Genomströmningen går ihop: "En granskning som tog omkring tre minuter tar sju." och "En sköterska som hann fyrtio barn under en förmiddag på två timmar hinner sjutton." - 120/3 = 40 och 120/7 = 17,1, alltså sjutton. Båda leden stämmer.
justification: D är den orsak texten själv pekar ut; A motsägs av att ingen rad prövas om, B av att raderna uttryckligen inte är det som tar tid, C av att även ett barn som stannar högt upp tar längre tid.

findings: Nyckel A stod uttryckt: "Det nya arket sattes upp i distriktens skolor under höstterminen 1978. Nedgången i kurvan ligger på det året. Den kommer inte som en lutning över några år, utan mellan två på varandra följande årgångar."
B dödad av "Som en enda kurva över barns syn i en svensk stad går den inte att läsa." och av "de mäter alltså inte samma sak"
C dödad av "Gränsen 0,8 ändrades inte vid bytet"
D dödad av "samma steg finns i de tre distriktens siffror var för sig"

Årsspannet går ihop: "trettiosex årgångar, 1961 till 1996" ger 1996-1961+1 = 36 årgångar, och "I de sjutton första årgångarna" (1961-1977) plus "I de nitton följande" (1978-1996) ger 17+19 = 36. Bytesåret 1978 är den artonde årgången, alltså den första i den andra gruppen, vilket stämmer med att nedgången ligger mellan två på varandra följande årgångar.

Storleksordningen går ihop: nio procent mot fem procent efter bytet, och valideringen "Hälften av dem läste en rad längre ned på det nya arket, en femtedel två rader." med "Ett barn som på den gamla tavlan hade stannat på 0,8 klarade på det nya oftast 1,0." - ett steg 0,8 till 1,0 är faktorn 1,25, exakt ett radsteg på det nya arket ("ungefär en fjärdedel större än raden under"). Konsekvent.

Den nya trappan går ihop: fjorton rader ger tretton steg, och 1,25 upphöjt till 13 är ungefär 20, vilket matchar "mellan dem ändras storleken med en faktor tjugo"; 73 mm delat med 20 är 3,65 mm, alltså "den nedersta knappt fyra", och visus 0,1 gånger 20 ger "Nedersta raden svarar mot visus 2,0." Hela stegen, radantalet, faktorn och visusvärdet stämmer mot varandra.
justification: A återger textens egen beskrivning av nedgången; B motsägs av att serien inte går att läsa som en synkurva, C av att gränsen inte ändrades, D av att steget finns i alla tre distrikten var för sig.

findings: Nyckel D stod uttryckt: "Jag begär något annat: att stämman beslutar två saker i samma beslut. Först att uttagen sätts upp, gärna många och gärna svaga. Sedan i vilken ordning bilarna får ström de nätter då sju är fullt." plus "Vilken ordningen ska bli överlåter jag åt stämman."
C dödad av "Att den ska stå skriven innan uttagen sitter uppe är däremot hela min poäng." - C skjuter upp turordningen till när den behövs, vilket är precis det skribenten avvisar.
B dödad av "Någon större huvudsäkring tänker jag därför inte begära i år."
A dödad av "Men delningen har en botten." och av räkneexemplet "Delar vi fyrtiofem lika på tio bilar blir det fyra och en halv på var, och då laddar ingen av de tio."

Amperetalen går ihop: 125 A huvudsäkring minus cirka 80 A för huset ger "Det lämnar fyrtiofem ampere till bilarna"; 45/6 = 7,5, alltså "Sju bilar kan dela på vårt utrymme en natt."; 45/10 = 4,5 vilket ligger under sexampere-botten; 4 gånger 32 = 128, vilket matchar "Fyra sådana vill ha hundratjugoåtta ampere, och vi har fyrtiofem." och 128 överstiger dessutom hela husets huvudsäkring. Slutsatsen "De fyra stolparna är alltså snabba bara så länge tre av dem står tomma." stämmer: en stolpe på 32 A ryms i 45 A, två gör det inte.
Ingen dödsdom vilar enbart på slutledning i denna fråga.
justification: D är skribentens uttalade yrkande, ord för ord. C faller på att turordningen ska stå skriven innan uttagen sitter uppe, B på att hon inte begär större huvudsäkring i år, A på att lika delning under sex ampere gör att ingen laddar.

findings: Nyckel C stod uttryckt: "styrelsens förslag står där som punkt sju"
A dödad av "Kallelsen sitter med häftstift på anslagstavlan utanför tvättstugan"
B dödad av "Punkten är en rad lång"
D dödad av "Var de ska stå framgår inte."
Ingen dödsdom vilar enbart på slutledning i denna fråga.
justification: C står ordagrant i texten; A, B och D motsägs var för sig av en utskriven sats om anslagstavlan, om punktens längd och om att placeringen inte framgår.

findings: Nyckel D stod uttryckt: "och det skymmer inte sikten. Från gräset utanför ser man golvet från kant till kant." tillsammans med "Ett räcke i knähöjd"
A dödad av "Ett räcke i knähöjd är inte byggt för att hålla någon ute"
B dödad av "Räcket är det ursprungliga."
C dödad av "Insidan har sin gamla gröna färg i behåll."
Årtalen går ihop: "Börje Ängman, 1934" plus "tjugo somrar med folk som stod i gräset" landar i mitten av femtiotalet, vilket stämmer med "det har inte dansats på den sedan femtiotalet"
justification: D återger den utsatta följden av räckets knähöjd; A motsägs av att det inte är byggt för att hålla någon ute, B av att räcket är det ursprungliga, C av den bevarade gröna färgen på insidan.

findings: Nyckel A i två led. Enkelriktningen: "paren går åt samma håll, motsols" och "Alltså ligger trafiken i ett band längs kanten." med "I ett fyrkantigt golv är hörnen just det som bandet inte kan följa." och "En rund bana har ingen sådan punkt." Kostnaden: "Rundningen var inte det billiga valet: den kostade virke, för brädorna i kanten fick sågas krokiga och spillet blev stort."
B dödad av "Banan ligger under bar himmel, utan tak och utan stolpar inne på golvet."
C dödad av "längst bort på banan hördes de sämre"
D dödad av "Golvet ligger plant på sina syllar, och regnet rinner ner mellan brädorna."
Ingen dödsdom vilar enbart på slutledning i denna fråga.
justification: A täcker båda leden som texten anger: den enkelriktade trafiken längs kanten och att rundningen var det dyrare valet. B, C och D motsägs var för sig av en utskriven sats om tak och stolpar, om hörbarheten och om att golvet ligger plant.
